title: Gideon and the Harvest
premise: Oscar Marchetti returns to the dying farm town of Harrow Bend to settle their grandmother's estate and finds Gideon—the imaginary friend who vanished when they were nine—waiting on the porch, unchanged after twenty years. The tunnels beneath the property hum an old harvest song, sung by the town's founders to feed something in the dark, and every heir of the Marchetti line is expected to learn the final verse that binds the singer to it forever. As neighbors who once seemed kind reveal themselves as keepers of the rite, Oscar must decide whether loyalty to their family's buried history matters more than the truth that could free the town. In the end, Oscar learns the last verse but refuses to sing it, instead teaching it back to the thing below—unmaking the bargain at the cost of Gideon's existence and nearly their own mind.
about_author: Ansel Zhou is a former land surveyor from rural Ohio whose maps kept showing features no one had drawn before. They write horror about places that remember more than the people living in them.

chapters.title: The Porch Light
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Returning to Harrow Bend for the funeral and estate reading, Oscar finds the farmhouse exactly as they left it—and Gideon, ageless, sitting on the porch steps as if twenty years never passed. The beat is uncanny dread wrapped in terrible nostalgia.

chapters.title: Estate of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The lawyer reads a will full of strange conditions: Oscar must remain on the property through harvest season or forfeit everything. A neighbor, Mrs. Aldous, watches the house too closely. Beat: gilded trap, unease beneath grief.

chapters.title: Gideon's Rules
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Gideon reappears inside the house despite locked doors, cheerful and wrong, listing rules: don't sing past sundown, don't answer knocking from below, never go into the cellar alone. Beat: childhood comfort curdling into control.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, flashbacks interleaved. Oscar digs out their old urban-exploration maps and realizes the tunnel entrances they found at nine match lines they once drew as 'imaginary.' Beat: the past was evidence all along.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve Potluck
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the town potluck, everyone sings a round song Oscar almost remembers; when they hum along, conversations stop mid-sentence. Mrs. Aldous warns them gently to leave before the season turns. Beat: belonging offered with a hook in it.

chapters.title: Knocking From Below
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Something knocks up through the cellar floor in rhythm—three slow, three fast—matching a pattern from Oscar's childhood games with Gideon. They don't open the hatch. Beat: white-knuckle restraint, dread compounding.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In a locked trunk, Oscar finds ledgers: generations of Marchettis recording verses learned, verses refused, and names struck through. Their grandmother's last entry is unfinished. Beat: inheritance revealed as debt.

chapters.title: The Song Has Five Verses
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV with Gideon present. Gideon teaches verses one through four willingly, sweet-voiced, but goes silent and glassy whenever Oscar asks about the fifth. Beat: seduction of knowledge, first real fear of the friend.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldous's Confession
chapters.summary: Mrs. Aldous's POV. She explains the founding families sang the thing below asleep each autumn; a Marchetti must always be among the singers, and her own son refused the verse thirty years ago and was 'harvested.' Beat: tragic exposition, stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Trespass
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Ignoring the rules, Oscar enters the cellar hatch and follows humming air into unmapped tunnels, finding walls carved with thousands of names—including MARCHETTI, over and over, freshest at the bottom. Beat: transgression and awe.

chapters.title: The First Refusal
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, young Oscar's POV. Twelve years ago: the night nine-year-old Oscar stopped singing with Gideon, the noises began, and Gideon 'went away'—or was taken as payment deferred. Beat: guilt reframed; the reader learns Oscar caused this.

chapters.title: Sundown Chorus
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. On the equinox, the whole town gathers at the field edge and sings; the ground answers. Oscar feels their mouth moving without permission and bites through their lip to stop. Beat: loss of bodily autonomy, horror of complicity.

chapters.title: Gideon's Hunger
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Gideon begins appearing gaunt, pleading, insisting the fifth verse is mercy—that the thing below only wants to be remembered properly. His face flickers between child and something older. Beat: manipulation wearing love's mask.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mrs. Aldous's POV. She shows Oscar the keepers' master book: every verse ever taught, and a marginal note in the founder's hand—the fifth verse doesn't bind the singer to the thing; it binds the thing to the singer. Beat: revelation that flips the power dynamic.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Townsfolk begin pressuring Oscar openly; crops fail early, animals die facing the house. Old friend Dale begs them to just sing, arguing tradition has kept everyone alive for two centuries. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: Descent With a Lantern
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Armed with the founder's note, Oscar returns to the tunnels to find the source, following Gideon's fading voice. They find the chamber: not a monster but a vast, starving presence woven from every verse ever sung into it. Beat: awe and pity replacing terror.

chapters.title: The Bargain Restated
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The presence offers Oscar a trade: sing the fifth verse and Gideon lives whole, the town prospers, and Oscar becomes its keeper forever—or refuse and watch it take the town's singers one by one. Beat: the devil's arithmetic, genuine temptation.

chapters.title: What Gideon Was
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He confesses he was the first Marchetti child, sung into the dark two hundred years ago and sent back up as a lure, generation after generation. He loves Oscar and was built to betray them. Beat: heartbreak; the imaginary friend was the first victim.

chapters.title: Learning the Last Verse
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar memorizes the fifth verse deliberately, silently, letting the town believe they've surrendered. Mrs. Aldous helps falsify the ledger entry. Beat: quiet resolve, the calm before the climax.

chapters.title: Harvest Night
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the final rite, with the town singing around them, Oscar opens their mouth—and sings the fifth verse backward, giving the words back to the thing below instead of binding themselves. The ground splits; the presence rises. Beat: climax, defiance at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Unmaking
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The returned verse unravels the bargain; the presence, finally remembered rather than fed, dissolves upward like seed husks in wind. Gideon holds Oscar's hand as he comes apart, thanking them, becoming a child again at the end. Beat: catharsis through grief.

chapters.title: After the Last Verse
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. Spring: the tunnels are gone from every map, the town half-empty but free, the farmhouse sold. Oscar keeps one page of the ledger blank and plants a garden where the hatch was. Final beat: mourning, freedom, and the choice to leave nothing inherited behind.
